ansur_standing_anchors_at_182_mm.definitions: standing living skin landmarks above the floor; prediction and residual SD

thorax_pitch_conflict.reading: Both bony models put C7 about 33-46 mm above IJ (IJ-C7 line about 20 deg); 4,082 standing men put the skin landmarks 80.7 +/- 11.4 mm apart. Either the generic/specimen thoraces are pitched differently from standing men, or skin landmarks differ from the bony points. The standing thorax pitch, and therefore the global ISB thorax axes, stays OPEN.

vertebral_level_line.source: Razzouk et al. 2023 (J Clin Neurosci): sternal notch at the T2-T3 vertebral bodies in CT of 1,035 patients (supine); abstract level
vertebral_level_line.basis: registered level stack (C7, T1, T2, T3 bodies; C7/T1, T1/T2, T2/T3 discs)
vertebral_level_line.reading: The C7 body centre sits about 48-58 mm above the notch along the spine. The C7 spinous tip lies below its body centre by an UNSOURCED amount (spinous processes slope caudally), so this line supports a bony C7-tip-above-IJ of well under 58 mm, in line with the bony models and against the 80.7 mm living skin value. It is supine CT; standing may lower the sternum relative to the spine. Not resolved.

SC_relative_to_IJ.reading: SC is close to IJ, so pitch uncertainty of +/-20 deg moves its height relative to IJ by only a few mm; its absolute height is dominated by the IJ height.

provisional_SC_height_mm.basis: ANSUR suprasternale at 1.82 m (skin; bony notch taken at the same height) plus Seth SC-above-IJ

a003.reading: a003 IJ (and SC with it) sits about 2 SD above the 1.82 m standard because it follows the authored r95 sternal notch; under the owner policy the canonical IJ follows the standard. a003 SC breadth matches the model breadth.
